images.title: A rhombus with a 50° angle
images.purpose: Shows rhombus ABCD with ∠A = 50° whose diagonal BD makes four equal 65° angles, so the angles are 50°, 130°, 50° and 130°.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large rhombus in the centre lying on its side, one diagonal drawn, and the angle sizes marked.
images.exact_structure: One rhombus in dark outline lying flat, about 2.1 times as wide as it is tall, with the sharp corners at left and right: A at the left (sharp, 50°), B at the top, C at the right (sharp, 50°), D at the bottom. Each of the four sides carries one identical short tick mark. The diagonal BD is a thick teal (#0072B2) vertical line from top to bottom. A small amber (#E69F00) arc labelled 50° at the left corner and at the right corner. At the top corner two small reddish purple (#CC79A7) arcs, one on each side of the diagonal, each labelled 65°. At the bottom corner one larger reddish purple arc labelled 130°. No corner letters are shown. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: In a rhombus with a 50° angle, the diagonal makes 65° and 65°, so the angles are 50°, 130°, 50° and 130°.
images.description: Shows rhombus ABCD with ∠A = 50° whose diagonal BD makes four equal 65° angles, so the angles are 50°, 130°, 50° and 130°.

image_decisions.why: The diagonal's two equal 65° parts show how the 130° angle comes from the isosceles triangle.
